blocks.content: The Document Kit: five self-contained, importable first-party plugins for document creation, each a plugin.json manifest plus a dependency-free stdio MCP server following the example-text-formatter pattern. doc-text (write_markdown/write_text/write_html with a shared Markdown→HTML converter), doc-email (create_email_template with {{variables}} → create_eml rendering multipart plain+HTML), doc-pdf (create_pdf — hand-rolled PDF writer: Letter pages, Helvetica + Helvetica-Bold, approximate-metric word wrap, automatic pagination, Latin-1 sanitization), doc-spreadsheets (create_xlsx — hand-rolled ZIP writer with CRC-32 + minimal Office Open XML parts, inline strings and numbers, multiple named sheets — plus RFC-4180 create_csv), doc-presentations (create_pptx — minimal OOXML part set: presentation + master + layout + theme + slides).

The tools reject lexical traversal and detected symlink escapes for output paths (and email template reads); Markdown-to-HTML links reject unsafe schemes; email variable CR/LF is stripped; CSV formula-leading values are escaped. This is defense-in-depth, not a sandbox: plugins are ordinary local processes and path checks retain a TOCTOU race. Nothing is sent anywhere (the .eml files are opened by the user's own mail client). Independent current test run: 57 document-plugin assertions pass; QuickLook previously rendered sample PDF/XLSX/PPTX, but cross-platform application compatibility is unverified. Samples: node tests/generate-doc-samples.mjs.
Named sheets of string/number rows → real .xlsx.
Template .md with metadata header + {{vars}} → rendered .eml (never sent).
